title: Knowledge check: Form Control Sizing and States

questions.prompt: Which item is explicitly covered by “Form Control Sizing and States” in the source syllabus?
options: Relationship between HTML, CSS, and JavaScript
questions.explanation: The syllabus lists “Small and large controls” under “Form Control Sizing and States”. Apply this topic in the lesson example and confirm its actual browser behavior.

questions.prompt: When applying form control sizing and states in a real interface, which approach is the strongest default?
options: Use the documented pattern, preserve semantic HTML, and test the relevant state.
Use color alone to communicate meaning and skip text labels.
Assume a visible style automatically provides application behavior.
Load multiple Bootstrap JavaScript builds to ensure each control works.
questions.answer_key: Use the documented pattern, preserve semantic HTML, and test the relevant state.
questions.explanation: Prefer documented conventions and semantic markup. Verify responsive and interaction behavior, accessibility, and runtime assumptions instead of relying on appearance alone.

questions.prompt: Which verification step best complements a lesson on form control sizing and states?
options: Record the expected result, reproduce the relevant state, and test the change at a second viewport or interaction state.
Publish the result after checking only the default viewport.
Remove all labels and focus indicators to reduce visual clutter.
Trust the CSS class name without checking the loaded Bootstrap version.
questions.answer_key: Record the expected result, reproduce the relevant state, and test the change at a second viewport or interaction state.
questions.explanation: A repeatable check compares expected and actual behavior and includes a relevant viewport or interaction state. Document what was checked and what still needs review.
